title: Harness OS bundle (.hos.json)
description: A portable, storable, swappable package of a harness OS. The bundle is a packaging layer ON TOP of the live .claude/harness-os.json the kernel reads: it wraps the manifest with identity (name@revision), provenance, and an integrity fingerprint, so a designed OS can be exported to a library, shared, version-pinned, diffed, and swapped in and out of a project as one unit. Runtime state (.claude/harness-os.state/) is NEVER part of a bundle — a bundle is a definition, not a running instance. Produced/consumed by the harness-os CLI (export/import/list/use/status).

kind.description: Discriminator identifying this file as a harness OS bundle.

bundleVersion.description: Envelope format version (distinct from manifest.harnessOsVersion, which is the contract the kernel enforces). A reader refuses envelope versions it does not understand.

name.description: Stable identifier of this OS, independent of any single project. Together with revision it is the library key (<name>@<revision>.hos.json).

revision.description: Version of this OS definition. Semver (1.2.0) or a plain integer string. Bumping it on every meaningful change is what makes swaps unambiguous and rollbacks possible.

createdAt.description: RFC3339 timestamp stamped by the CLI at export.

basedOn.description: Lineage: the template or bundle name this OS was derived from, if any.

manifest.description: The harness OS role manifest itself — the exact document written to .claude/harness-os.json on import. Validated against harness-os.schema.json independently (by the CLI and the fixture linter); embedded here verbatim so a bundle is self-contained. Kept as a plain object here so the two schemas stay decoupled — the manifest contract lives in harness-os.schema.json alone.

fingerprint.description: Integrity + identity hash of the embedded manifest: 'sha256:' + hex sha256 of the manifest canonicalised as JSON with all object keys sorted recursively and no insignificant whitespace. Recomputed on import and by `status`; a mismatch between this value and the live .claude/harness-os.json means the manifest drifted from the stored bundle. Deterministic across machines.

notes.description: Free-form changelog / design rationale for this revision.

assets.description: Optional companion files shipped with a directory-form bundle (<name>@<rev>/), addressed by relative path — e.g. per-role brief templates the orchestrator pastes into dispatch prompts, or a README. Advisory: the kernel never reads these; they travel with the OS for the humans and orchestrators who operate it.
